s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy, erythematous to violaceous skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Multiple milia in the superficial dermis on histopathologic examination
Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene identified on whole-exome sequencing

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic, progressive, itchy, erythematous to violaceous skin lesions with dermoepidermal separation and milia
salient_findings: Multiple itchy erythematous to violaceous papules and plaques on the left shin
Milia and erosions with partially detached epidermis
key_facts: Female patient in her 30s
Symptoms have been present for more than 10 years
Lesions are localized to the left shin
No abnormalities of the mucous membranes, nails, hair, or teeth
No extracutaneous involvement
Histopathologic examination revealed dermoepidermal separation
Multiple milia in the superficial dermis on histopathologic examination
Novel heterozygous missense variant in COL7A1 gene identified on whole-exome sequencing

differentials: chronic neutrophilic leukemia associated with csf3r mutation

raw.rationale: The presence of dermoepidermal separation and milia on histopathologic examination, along with the identification of a novel heterozygous missense variant in the COL7A1 gene, supports the diagnosis of bullous pemphigoid, which is a chronic autoimmune skin disease characterized by blistering and often associated with genetic variants affecting collagen and adhesion molecules.

rejected.label: lichen planus pemphigoides
rejected.why: While it shares some clinical features, the specific histopathologic findings and genetic variant point more strongly towards bullous pemphigoid

rejected.label: segmental infantile hemangioma with milia
rejected.why: The patient's age and the chronic nature of the condition do not align with this diagnosis, which typically presents in infancy

rejected.label: dermatitis
rejected.why: The histopathologic findings of dermoepidermal separation and milia are not typical of dermatitis

rejected.label: eczema
rejected.why: Eczema does not typically present with dermoepidermal separation or the specific genetic variant identified
